facts.statement: The species Dagasuchus santacruzensis was named in 2015 based on a partial hip consisting of one ilium and a pair of ischia discovered near Santa Cruz do Sul, Brazil.
facts.quote: D. santacruzensis was named in 2015 on the basis of specimen UFRGS-PV-1244-T and UFRGS-PV-1245-T, a partial hip (one ilium and a pair of ischia) found in an exposure of the Santa Maria Formation in the Paraná Basin, near the city of Santa Cruz do Sul.

facts.statement: Dagasuchus lived during the Late Triassic (Carnian) period in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
facts.quote: Dagasuchus is an extinct genus of pseudosuchian archosaur from the Late Triassic (Carnian) of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil

facts.statement: Dagasuchus is classified as an early member of the evolutionary group Loricata, which contains modern crocodilians and their ancestors.
facts.quote: Dagasuchus is an early member of a large evolutionary group called Loricata, which originated in the Triassic and includes modern crocodylians and their ancestors.

facts.statement: The hip structure of Dagasuchus closely resembles that of other early loricatans like Stagonosuchus and Saurosuchus.
facts.quote: Features of its hip closely resemble those of other early loricatans such as Stagonosuchus and Saurosuchus.

facts.statement: Dagasuchus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Dagasuchus is notable for being the first loricatan discovered in the Santacruzodon assemblage zone, filling a gap in the fossil record between older and younger zones where the group was previously known.
rejected.quote: Dagasuchus is notable for being the first loricatan found in the Santacruzodon assemblage zone of the Santa Maria Formation; previously loricatans were only known from the older Dinodontosaurus assemblage zone and the younger Hyperodapedon assemblage zone within the Santa Maria Formation, meaning that Dagasuchus fills in a gap in the fossil record of the group.
